claims.text: Sarathi-Serve (OSDI 2024) splits a prefill into near-equal-sized chunks and builds batches that add new prefill work without pausing the decodes already running, which it calls stall-free batching.
Sarathi-Serve picks its token budget from the latency target for the time between tokens: the largest chunk whose step still meets it.

The DistServe paper defines per-GPU goodput as the highest request rate that can be served while meeting an SLO attainment goal, such as 90% of requests meeting their TTFT and TPOT targets, for each GPU provisioned.

checks.method: browser: verbatim section text

claims.text: It argues that systems tuned for overall throughput, tokens per second across all users, must over-provision GPUs to meet latency targets.

checks.method: browser: verbatim section text

claims.text: NVIDIA lists the H100 SXM at 1,979 teraFLOPS of BF16 with sparsity, 3.35 TB/s of memory bandwidth and 80 GB of memory.
The DistServe paper argues that chunked prefill trades TTFT for TPOT and cannot remove the interference between the two phases.
